#MSNews | The Manila Police District (MPD) on Monday (May 18, 2026) confirmed its recommendation for preliminary investigation of 9 individuals over alleged public order violations in relation with the May 1 protest rally in Ermita, Manila.

“Our police personnel are mandated to exercise maximum tolerance. However, when the actions of certain individuals cross the line into unlawfulness and create undue tumult or danger to the public and our police officers, the MPD will not hesitate to enforce the law," Acting District Director PBGEN Arnold Santiago said. 

It can be recalled that some protesters allegedly became unruly and attempted to breach barricades. Meanwhile, one protester allegedly punched a police officer in the face, robbed a cellular phone used for field documentation, and physically assaulted police personnel, resulting in multiple injuries. | via Pot Chavez

For more details please visit https://t.co/rmQCnNSOvI

data.raw_text:
“Protest rallies are now ongoing in Cotabato City following the impending dismissal of BARMM Minister of Basic Higher and Technical Education Mohagher Iqbal by Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua. 

If this situation is not handled with wisdom, restraint, and genuine dialogue, it could escalate into violence and bloodshed within the ranks of the MILF, and may even drag the Armed Forces of the Philippines once again into renewed armed hostilities in Mindanao.

Should conflict erupt, the national government in Manila must bear responsibility for the consequences. Instead of respecting the spirit of autonomy and allowing the BARMM to govern its own affairs independently, the central government continues to interfere through divide-and-rule politics, particularly in the appointment and removal of key ministers and officials.

Peace in Mindanao cannot survive under political manipulation. Lasting peace requires respect for autonomy, sincerity in governance, and non-interference in the internal political processes of the Bangsamoro people.

//Romeo V Poquiz

IN PHOTOS: Members of various progressive, loyalist, sectoral, and pro-BBM organizations gather in front of the Senate of the Philippines during a “Jericho March” protest, renewing calls for justice, accountability, and the integrity of democratic institutions. The mobilization was led by groups under ALAB NG BAYAN, including the Filipinos Do Not Yield (FDNY) Movement, KAMASKARA, ABKD, LIPI, PADER, and several community-based organizations. 

📸: Norman Cruz
